title: KLEE symbolic VM
description: KLEE executes LLVM bitcode with symbolic inputs, forking a state at every symbolic branch and asking the solver which paths are feasible. It generated high-coverage test suites for real utilities (Coreutils) automatically — each path's constraints solved into concrete test inputs that drive down that exact path.
method: Interpret LLVM with symbolic values; fork on branches; query STP/Z3 for feasibility; solve path constraints into test inputs.
usage: Mark inputs symbolic; bound loops; use KLEE's output as a generated test suite.

demo.code:
print('symbolic: if (x > 10) ...')
print('fork: path1 {x > 10} -> test x=11; path2 {x <= 10} -> test x=5')

title: Environment modeling
description: Real programs call the environment — files, network, syscalls. Symbolic executors model these (symbolic files in KLEE, models of libc) so analysis doesn't stop at the first read() call. Good environment models are what separate toy demos from tools that handle real code.
method: Model syscalls/files symbolically; keep models faithful but simple; concretize where modeling is infeasible.
usage: Invest in models for the syscalls your target uses; document model limitations as analysis caveats.

demo.code:
print('read(fd, buf, n): symbolic file returns symbolic bytes')
print('analysis continues past I/O instead of stopping')

title: Under-constrained symbolic execution
description: Full-program symbolic execution drowns in environment complexity; under-constrained execution analyzes one function in isolation with symbolic inputs and lazy initialization of pointers. It finds real bugs in individual functions fast — trading whole-program soundness for targeted bug hunting.
method: Start at the target function; inputs fully symbolic; lazily initialize pointed-to memory; report bugs with the under-constrained caveat.
usage: Use for triaging suspicious functions; confirm findings with more precise analysis.

demo.code:
print('analyze parse_header() alone: inputs symbolic')
print('found: null deref on malformed header -> confirmed in full context')

title: Binary symbolic execution (angr)
description: angr lifts binaries to VEX IR and symbolically executes without source — finding bugs in firmware, CTF binaries, and closed-source code. Binary-level analysis handles what source tools can't: stripped binaries, inline assembly, and obfuscated code.
method: Lift to VEX IR; symbolic execution over IR; hook syscalls/library calls; solve for inputs reaching target addresses.
usage: Use for binary-only targets; hook environment interactions; verify findings concretely.

demo.code:
print('angr: find input reaching 0x401234 (vuln site)')
print('solver: input = b"AAAA..." (128 bytes) -> reaches target: CONFIRMED')

title: Veritesting (static+dynamic merge)
description: Veritesting statically merges straight-line code regions into single path constraints, so the dynamic engine forks only at genuinely hard branches. Developed for the Mayhem system (CMU), it tames path explosion in binary analysis by letting static analysis do the easy merging.
method: Statically recover CFG; merge bounded regions into formulas; dynamic execution handles the rest; fewer forks, same coverage.
usage: Use for binary analysis at scale; the static recovery quality bounds the benefit.

demo.code:
print('function: 200 branches, mostly straight-line')
print('veritesting merges 180 statically -> dynamic forks only 20')

title: Guided symbolic execution toward targets
description: Instead of exploring everywhere, directed symbolic execution aims at a target — a patched line, a dangerous sink, a crash site. Distance metrics on the CFG guide the search; the solver only works on paths that can reach the target. Bug hunting with a destination.
method: Compute CFG distance to target; prioritize states by distance; prune states that can't reach the target; solve on arrival.
usage: Define targets precisely (line numbers, sink calls); combine with patch-diff to check only changed code's reachability.

demo.code:
print('target: memcpy at line 88 (patched)')
print('guided search: 12 states pruned, target reached in 40s')
print('input reaching patch: generated for regression test')

title: Symbolic execution for test generation
description: Every explored path yields concrete inputs that drive that path — an automatic high-coverage test suite. KLEE on Coreutils found real bugs and generated tests no human wrote. For parsers, protocols, and utilities, symbolic test generation beats hand-written tests on coverage per effort.
method: Explore paths; solve each path's constraints; emit (input, expected-path) as tests; minimize the suite.
usage: Generate, minimize, and check in the suite; re-generate when the code changes significantly.

demo.code:
print('parser: 47 paths explored -> 47 tests generated')
print('coverage: 96% branches (hand-written suite: 71%)')

title: SMT solver integration
description: The solver is the engine's oracle: every branch feasibility check, every test-input generation is an SMT query. Solver choice and query shaping (incremental solving, constraint caching, independent-constraint splitting) determine whether the engine runs for minutes or days.
method: Incremental solver sessions; cache query results; split independent constraints; choose solver per theory (bitvectors vs arrays).
usage: Profile solver time first when the engine is slow; enable caching and incremental modes.

demo.code:
print('query cache hit rate 78% -> solver time 41min -> 9min')
print('independent constraint splitting: 3 sub-queries, parallel')
